chunks: God has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a means of support for mankind, as also the holy month, the sacrificial offerings, and consecrated cattle, so that you may understand that known to God is all that is in the heavens and the earth, and God has knowledge of everything.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Ka'bah and sacred month in demonstrating God's knowledge?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Ma'idah underscores the Ka'bah as the primordial axis of unity (al-Qiblah al-Ula) and the sacred month as a period of truce, reflecting God's sovereignty over both ritual and social order. The mention of 'hady' (sacrificial camels) and 'qalaid' (garlands) highlights the tangible signs of devotion, serving to remind believers that these physical acts are rooted in the Divine's absolute knowledge of the unseen, a theme central to Imam Ali's teachings on the inner reality of worship.
